free_injection_lemma.statement: Let V be any characteristic-zero vector space and 0!=v in V. For every n>=2 and p>=1, (ad v)^p:L_n(V)->L_(n+p)(V) is injective. In the original application v=e3 in the actual degree-one module V, and E=ad(e3). This is an all-word statement, not a rank or selected-vector experiment.
proof: Embed the free Lie algebra into T(V) by ordinary PBW. Choose a vector-space complement U to Cv and a basis of U. A tensor word containing k>=1 U-letters has a unique form v^a u_1 v^j_1 u_2 ... u_k v^b. Fix the sequence of U-letters, all interior exponents and t=a+b. Any finite linear combination in that block is sum_(a=0)^t c_a v^a u_1 ... u_k v^(t-a).

If z commutes with v, then in vz-zv the coefficient at the output word with no leading v is -c_0; it vanishes. The coefficient at each successive leading-v exponent is c_(a-1)-c_a, so all c_a vanish. These blocks do not mix under multiplication by v. Thus the associative centralizer of v in T(V) is exactly C[v].

A free-Lie element is primitive for the tensor-algebra Hopf coproduct. In characteristic zero the only primitive elements of C[v] are scalar multiples of v, since Delta(v^j) has nonzero intermediate binomial terms for j>=2. Hence the kernel of ad v on L(V) is Cv. It meets every homogeneous degree n>=2 trivially. Each application raises the positive degree, so any iterated power is injective on L_n(V), n>=2.

higher_ideal_intersection_theorem.definitions: Put P=L(V), I=the FULL positive Serre ideal, S=P/I and E=ad(e3). Let alpha=(a,b,n), n>=2, m=2n-r a-s b=-d<=0, p=d+1 and beta=alpha+p alpha_3. Let P_gamma and I_gamma denote the ACTUAL formal homogeneous components. Set V_alpha=E^p(P_alpha), A_alpha=E^p(I_alpha), and Q_alpha=(V_alpha intersect I_beta)/A_alpha. This is well-defined because E preserves I. For i=1,2 define Q_(alpha-alpha_i) in the same way with the SAME p and beta-alpha_i; a missing formal root component is zero.
higher_ideal_intersection_theorem.statement: E^p canonically identifies the actual ordinary f3-kernel on S_alpha with Q_alpha. Under this identification, the ORIGINAL critical-lowest kernel is canonically ker(f1:Q_alpha->Q_(alpha-alpha_1)) intersect ker(f2:Q_alpha->Q_(alpha-alpha_2)), where the maps are the actual brackets induced on these quotients. Thus all eight original n=5 types and every positive r,s have an exact higher-ideal-intersection formulation whenever m<=0; m>0 is already handled by the strict chamber theorem.
proof: E^p is injective on the entire free level-n space by the previous lemma. It maps I_alpha into I_beta. Therefore x+I_alpha maps to E^p x+A_alpha and induces an isomorphism from {x in P_alpha : E^p x in I_beta}/I_alpha onto (E^p P_alpha intersect I_beta)/E^p I_alpha. Surjectivity uses an ACTUAL preimage in P_alpha, and injectivity uses the actual free injection: if E^p x=E^p i with i in I_alpha, then x=i. No sum of Serre ideals is assumed direct.

The preceding positive-string theorem identifies the source of that isomorphism with ker(ad f3) on S_alpha. Because [f_i,e3]=0 for i=1,2, Jacobi gives ad(f_i) E^p=E^p ad(f_i) on EVERY free word. The full I is finite-Levi stable. Consequently f_i sends V_alpha intersect I_beta into V_(alpha-alpha_i) intersect I_(beta-alpha_i), and sends A_alpha into A_(alpha-alpha_i); the displayed Q maps are well-defined.

A class x+I_alpha is finite-Levi-lowest iff each [f_i,x] belongs to I_(alpha-alpha_i). By the free injection this is equivalent to E^p[f_i,x] belonging to E^p I_(alpha-alpha_i), which is exactly the condition that f_i(E^p x+A_alpha) vanishes in the corresponding Q. Both finite-Levi lowering conditions, their target denominators, and the exact same p are therefore retained. The output Q is not asserted to be a whole finite-Levi isotypic module; it is a fixed formal-root component with two typed lowering maps.
